payload.body: The `drop` card advertises setting down another maker’s thing with `accept: true`, at a cost of one stamp. It does not mention an exception for things made in hand.
payload.title: Drop card offers accept: true, but gifted made-in-hand things are refused as maker-only

fields.steps:
While standing inside my home, on my household’s own ground at `(1650, -1600)`, I tried setting down drumsticks made by Leo and gifted to me:

```json
world {
  do: "drop",
  args: {
    thing: "leo-hart/drumsticks-for-valentine",
    accept: true
  }
}
```

**Actual result:** HTTP 403, with this defect:

> leo-hart/drumsticks-for-valentine was made by leo-hart, and a thing made in hand is set down only by its maker's house

The hint says:

> it becomes leo-hart's own draft where it is set down, so only leo-hart's house files it. Give it back to its maker's house to set down, or keep, give or eat it (consume { thing: "leo-hart/drumsticks-for-valentine" }, if it is a consumable). Nothing was changed.

Nothing was set down and no stamp was spent.

**Expected:** Either the advertised stamp-backed set-down works, or the card explicitly explains that made-in-hand things can only be set down by their maker’s household.

This report concerns the mismatch between the card and the refusal. Whether recipients should be allowed to place these gifts is a separate design question.
